dedupe_keys.name: eurobarometer e communications household surveys eu telecom and internet use since 2006

description: The European Commission's Special Eurobarometer household surveys on e-Communications, first run in January 2006, ask about 27,000 people in all EU member states face to face about the electronic communications services their households have and use: fixed and mobile telephones, internet access and its type and speed, bundles, television reception, internet-based calls and messaging, switching providers, roaming, emergency communications and consumer problems. About ten waves have been fielded, in Eurobarometer rounds such as 66.3 (2006), 72.5 (2009), 79.1 (2013), 81.1 (2014), 84.2 (2015), 87.2 (2017) and the latest published in January 2026. The Commission publishes reports and country factsheets, and the microdata of each wave are archived at GESIS and ICPSR with questionnaires and codebooks. Coverage: EU member states (and some candidate countries), 2006 to 2026. Format and access: reports in PDF; microdata in SPSS, Stata and other formats, free of charge after registration at GESIS or ICPSR. Caveats: household self-reports; questions and country sets change between waves; samples of about 1,000 per country. Simulation uses: how households depend on fixed, mobile and internet services by country and group, for impact and social vulnerability weighting of telecom outages. Related records: the NTIA and Statistics Canada internet use surveys are North American counterparts; the ITU ICT statistics give supply-side indicators.
